title: To cover a permutohedron
abstract: This Lean 4 formalization of Kong and Zeng's To cover a permutohedron (arXiv:2509.13877v3, 9 April 2026) determines the minimum number of affine hyperplanes needed to cover the permutation vertices of (1,...,n), excluding the hyperplane containing every vertex. The exact answer is n for odd n at least 3, and n-1 for even n at least 4. It also proves that an arbitrary injective real tuple of length n at least 2 has the sharp hyperplane intersection bound (n-1)! when its n-1 signed critical values are distinct. Genuine polynomial-root path lifting establishes local transpositions and the cycle at infinity, with explicit corrections to the source's loop hypotheses. A symmetric polynomial norm replaces the paper's general Bezout step. One independent Challenge and one Comparator configuration cover all eighteen results, including sharp constructions, generic and four-element consequences, and the connection with convex vertices and arbitrary affine hyperplanes.
